item.title: RCSS Class of 2025 posts strong graduation outcomes across academic pathways
item.description: The Richmond County School System Class of 2025 recorded strong graduation outcomes across Georgia’s four academic pathway types. The post RCSS Class of 2025 posts strong graduation outcomes across academic pathways appeared first on The Augusta Press.

item.title: 16th annual Jimmie Dyess Symposium honors local heroes with tradition
item.description: The Jimmie Dyess Symposium, the Augusta Museum of History’s annual event recognizing recipients of the Distinguished American Award in honor of Augusta war hero Lt. Col. Jimmie Dyess, introduced a new element to its proceedings this year. The post 16th annual Jimmie Dyess Symposium honors local heroes with tradition appeared first on The Augusta Press.

item.title: Charter panel backs off Urban Services District, debates equal opportunity language
item.description: At a Thursday work session, Augusta’s Charter Review Committee touched on several topics Thursday including the Urban Services District and equal opportunity. The post Charter panel backs off Urban Services District, debates equal opportunity language appeared first on The Augusta Press.

item.title: Miami returns home, starts process of getting ready for CFP title game
item.description: A man drove past where the buses that carried the Miami Hurricanes back to their campus on Friday afternoon, windows rolled down on his vehicle and he was smiling as he honked his horn over and over and over again. The post Miami returns home, starts process of getting ready for CFP title game appeared first on The Augusta Press.

item.title: Brooks Koepka is out of LIV Golf. Now he has applied for PGA Tour membership again
item.description: Five-time major champion Brooks Koepka, just over two weeks after defecting from Saudi-funded LIV Golf, has applied to have his PGA Tour membership reinstated. The post Brooks Koepka is out of LIV Golf. Now he has applied for PGA Tour membership again appeared first on The Augusta Press.

item.title: No. 1 Indiana adds to CFP dominance with crushing 56-22 Peach Bowl semifinal win over No. 5 Oregon
item.description: Undefeated Indiana's already impressive march through the College Football Playoff gained momentum as its dominant defense created three first-half touchdowns with turnovers, Fernando Mendoza threw five scoring passes and the Hoosiers overwhelmed No. 5 Oregon 56-22 in the Peach Bowl semifinal on Friday night. The post No. 1 Indiana adds to CFP dominance with crushing 56-22 Peach Bowl semifinal win over No. 5 Oregon appeared first on The Augusta Press.

item.title: SRNS supports CSRA charitable organizations with $50,000 in giving
item.description: Savannah River Nuclear Solutions (SRNS) reaffirmed its commitment to the Central Savannah River Area (CSRA) during the holiday season by awarding five charitable organizations with $10,000 each, totaling $50,000 in community support. The post SRNS supports CSRA charitable organizations with $50,000 in giving appeared first on The Augusta Press.

item.title: Democratic hopefuls for governor stake out positions in first big forum
item.description: Most of the Democrats who say they are running for governor appeared in a forum televised from a Savannah church Thursday night, where they worked to differentiate themselves before a primary election just four months away. The post Democratic hopefuls for governor stake out positions in first big forum appeared first on The Augusta Press.

item.title: A quieter year on Richmond County’s streets: Sheriff Brantley touts drops in crime and fatal crashes
item.description: By the time the calendar closed on 2025, something unusual had happened in Richmond County: fewer lives were being lost to violence, and fewer families were getting the late-night knock that follows a fatal crash. The post A quieter year on Richmond County’s streets: Sheriff Brantley touts drops in crime and fatal crashes appeared first on The Augusta Press.
